chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha', from Dawud ibn Zurbi, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about wudu (ablution), and he said to me: "Perform wudu three times."

He said: Then he said to me: "Do you not witness Baghdad and their military camps?" I said: Yes. He said: "One day I was performing wudu in the house of al-Mahdi, and some of them saw me while I was unaware of him, so he said: 'Whoever claims that you are so-and-so has lied, while you perform this wudu.'" He said: So I said: "By Allah, for this reason he commanded me."
Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: There is no sunnah (prophetic tradition) in wiping the head and the feet more than once; rather, that one time is the obligation.
What indicates that is His, the Exalted's, statement:

Whoever wipes once has fallen within the apparent meaning, while anything beyond one time requires a legal proof. There is no legal proof here that wiping the head is more than a single pass, and most of the reports previously mentioned regarding the description of wudu also indicate that, because when they finished describing the washing of the limbs, they said: "and he wiped his head and his feet," and they did not say: one pass or two passes. Had it been more than that, they would have clarified it, and this further confirms that as well.

key_terms.الرَّأْسِ: the head, one of the places wiped in wudu
key_terms.الرِّجْلَيْنِ: the two feet, to be wiped in wudu
key_terms.السُّنَّةُ: the sunnah (prophetic tradition), here referring to what is legislated in practice
key_terms.الْمَسْحِ: wiping, specifically over the head and feet in wudu
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification being discussed
key_terms.دَلَالَةٍ شَرْعِيَّةٍ: legal proof from the Sacred Law

ai.seo_question: How many times should the head and feet be wiped in wudu according to this narration from Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This hadith reports an instruction about outwardly performing wudu in a manner suited to circumstances, followed by al-Shaykh's legal clarification that wiping the head and feet in wudu is only once. The argument is based on the Quranic wording and the descriptions found in the reports of wudu, which do not establish repetition in the mash.
